definition: Perspicacity means keen insight and sharp perceptiveness.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word perspicacity. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know perspicacity should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Veteran birders envied the guide's perspicacity: from one half-second flick of a wing she could name species, sex, and season.
Awareness just means the fact registered - you noticed the smile; perspicacity reads what the smile is hiding.
Insight is a single shaft of understanding; perspicacity goes further - the standing, reusable sharpness that produces insight after insight.

Acuity is raw sharpness — of eyesight, hearing, or intellect — the sheer resolution of the instrument. Perspicacity is what sharpness achieves when it is aimed: perception that penetrates surfaces and reads what is really going on. A hawk has acuity; a great detective has perspicacity.

Discernment is fine judgment in telling things apart — good from bad, real from fake, better from best. Perspicacity works one step earlier: it is the penetrating perception that sees what is actually there, handing discernment the material it will judge.

Astuteness is practical sharpness — reading a situation quickly and turning it to advantage, especially in bargaining and politics. Perspicacity is quieter and deeper: penetrating perception that sees through the surface to what is really going on, whether or not any advantage follows.

Its neighbor in this unit, sagacity, praises the judgment that follows: the perspicacious eye spots the trap, the sagacious mind decides what to do about it.
In plain speech, 'sharp' covers both.

Crews on the ridge saw a quiet flank of the fire, barely smoking, and radioed that the line would hold until morning.
Ana Reyes, the incident's fire-behavior analyst, read the same slope differently.
The smoke was thin, but it had begun to lean uphill against the evening wind — a small wrongness most eyes slide past.
Her perspicacity was not better eyesight; everyone could see the smoke.
It was knowing what the lean meant: heat building in the duff, a run being prepared under a calm surface.
She called for the crews to pull back to the creek.
Two hours later the flank crowned and took the ridge in minutes.
The after-action report gave one line to the save: the analyst saw what the fire was hiding.
